summary: Field runs SuperCollider's language interpreter, sclang, in two places: to render every supercollider: entry in field build, and to run the voice host that field keys plays an instrument through. Both find sclang with one function, sclangCommand in src/generators/supercollider.ts. On Windows that function could not find a real sclang even with SuperCollider installed, so renders and field keys stopped there.

This pull request makes the lookup platform-aware. On Windows it searches PATH for sclang.com and sclang.exe, reads a native FIELD_SCLANG such as C:\Program Files\SuperCollider-3.13.0\sclang.exe as a path, and falls back to the newest SuperCollider-<version> folder under Program Files. macOS and Linux keep the lookup they had. The platform becomes a parameter of sclangCommand, so a new test file runs the Windows rules on any machine.

Windows treats .bat and .cmd files as runnable too, but Node refuses to start them without a shell, and both callers start sclang without one. So the lookup never returns one, and a FIELD_SCLANG that names one is refused with a message that says Windows cannot start it directly.

cards.title: Where the lookup looks, in order
cards.html:
StepmacOS and LinuxWindows
FIELD_SCLANG setA value with / is a path; a bare name is searched on PATHA value with \, /, or : is a path; a bare name is searched on PATH as .com and .exe. Anything found that is not a .com or .exe is refused.
PATHsclang in each :-separated directorysclang.com, then sclang.exe, in each ;-separated directory, never the bare name
Installed copyThe app bundle, on macOS onlyThe newest SuperCollider-<version>\sclang.exe under ProgramFiles

A FIELD_SCLANG that names nothing is an error, never a fall through to the installed copy, so a mistyped wrapper cannot silently run a different sclang.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html:
• First review, at 603c3e1: changes requested, with two findings. The lookup could return a .cmd or .bat that Node will not start, and two new tests failed on the Windows CI job.
  • Fixes, in 70a690c and 3282661: the search tries only .com and .exe, a batch FIELD_SCLANG is refused with the reason, and the two POSIX-fixture tests skip on Windows. b2f19a0 also lets the real-sclang build test find sclang on Windows.
  • Second review, at b2f19a0: clean. Both findings were verified fixed, and it suggested rewording one refusal message.
  • Third review, at d1169c1: clean, incremental on the second. The refusal now reads which Windows cannot start directly, which is true for an extensionless file too, and a new test covers that case.
  • CI: the linux job passes. The windows job passes every lookup test, and fails only tests that also fail on other branches' Windows runs.

groups.title: The sclang lookup
groups.kicker: One function decides which sclang a render and the voice host run, now per platform.
intro: sclangCommand returns the path of the sclang to run. runScProgram starts it with execFile for a render, and VoiceHost.start starts it with spawn for field keys. Neither caller uses a shell, so on Windows the path must end in .com or .exe, the only files Node starts without one.

Three helpers carry the Windows rules. variable reads an environment variable without regard to case on Windows, because Windows spells PATH as Path and a copied environment loses the case-insensitive lookup that process.env has. onPath searches PATH, trying each of WINDOWS_EXECUTABLES on Windows. installedSclang finds the copy the SuperCollider installer put in place: the app bundle on macOS, or the newest versioned folder under Program Files on Windows.

checks.text: PATHEXT is the Windows list of extensions that the command shell treats as runnable, by default .COM;.EXE;.BAT;.CMD. The lookup does not read it. It tries .com and .exe only, because Node refuses .bat and .cmd without a shell and throws spawn EINVAL.

files.note: The platform-aware lookup: three new helpers, the WINDOWS_EXECUTABLES list, and a platform parameter on sclangCommand.

checks.text: macOS and Linux keep their behavior. I called the built sclangCommand with linux and darwin against temporary files, and it returned what main returns: a FIELD_SCLANG with / is a path, a bare name is searched on a :-split PATH, and only macOS falls back to the app bundle. The one difference is that Linux no longer checks the macOS bundle path, which cannot exist there.
Copied environments work. With the keys spelled Path and programfiles, the lookup still found sclang.exe in my probe.

Batch files never come back from the search. In my probe, a sclang.cmd and a sclang.bat earlier on PATH were passed over for sclang.exe, and with no .exe anywhere the lookup reported sclang not found. A PATHEXT that is empty or holds only .CMD changes nothing.

A FIELD_SCLANG that is not a .com or .exe is refused before anything starts. A .cmd or .BAT named by path, or a name with a .cmd extension found on PATH, reports which Windows cannot start directly. An uppercase .EXE passes.

The message reads true for every file it refuses: a .bat or .cmd, which Node will not start without a shell, and an extensionless file, which Windows cannot start at all. A search of src, docs, sc, and scripts finds no other reader of the old wording.
Versions sort as numbers. Under a fake Program Files holding SuperCollider-3.9, 3.10, 3.13.0, and an empty 3.14.0, the lookup returned 3.13.0.
ProgramW6432 is not read. Node publishes no 32-bit Windows build from version 23 on, so for field's process ProgramFiles already names the 64-bit folder.

groups.title: Tests for each platform's rules
groups.kicker: A new test file runs the Windows rules on any machine, and the real-sclang build test probes with the same lookup.
intro: Because sclangCommand takes the platform as a parameter, src/generators/supercollider.test.ts passes 'win32' or 'linux' and checks the result against real files in a temporary directory. That lets the macOS and Linux CI jobs run the Windows rules too.

The parameter does not change the host's own paths, though. Two tests build fixtures that only a POSIX host can hold, a drive path under the linux rule and a folder named C:, so they skip on a Windows host through onPosixHost. The linux job still runs them.

files.note: Eleven lookup tests, one per rule. Two skip on a Windows host; the other nine run everywhere.

checks.text: On macOS all 11 pass at d1169c1. On the windows CI job at b2f19a0, the 8 tests it had then ran and passed, and the 2 POSIX-fixture tests skipped.

These three tests cover the fix for the first review's finding. A sclang.cmd on PATH no longer shadows the installed sclang.exe, and a FIELD_SCLANG that names a batch file or an extensionless file is refused with the reason.

files.note: The real-sclang integration test now decides whether sclang is installed with sclangCommand, so it can run on Windows too.

checks.text: The supercollider and runScProgram edges tests pass on macOS: 7 run, with the real-sclang integration test left out.
The probe runs once, when the file loads, before any test sets FIELD_SCLANG. A FIELD_SCLANG that names nothing now skips the integration test, where the old probe ran it and failed.

groups.title: Docs and the plan
groups.kicker: The CLI manual, the keys guide, and the Windows plan describe the new order.
intro: docs/cli.md and docs/keys.md say where field build and field keys find sclang, now including sclang.exe and the Program Files folder. The Windows portability plan marks its §7.2 item, sclangCommand cannot find sclang on Windows, as ported.

checks.text: I read each doc change against sclangCommand at b2f19a0, and each matches the code. The plan stays in-progress, and project check passes.

files.note: The lookup order for renders, and the FIELD_SCLANG row of the environment table.
§7.2 records the item as ported, with the rules it now follows, including why the search leaves out the rest of PATHEXT.
